item.description: I was in the middle of writing yet another job application (#internship-grind) when one of friends messaged me telling I should just use an LLM to write it for me. My immediate response, as it is to most LLM related things, was “AAAAAAAA ughhhhhh I have feelings™️”1, prompting the reply “That’s not very 10x mindset of you” along with a link to an article from where he’s doing an internship. I jokingly replied “yeah I’m a 0.1x developer” (prompting the idea for this post), and then spent the rest of the day making a working compiler from scratch.

item.title: The GPU Is the New Storage Controller | Murat Karslioglu
item.description: For 40 years, the CPU decided what gets read from storage, when, and where it lands in memory. AI inference is breaking that model. The GPU now knows what data it needs next, and routing that request through the CPU is pure overhead. GPU-initiated I/O is the architectural response. But the protocol stack wasn't designed for it.

This is when we discovered the wonderful world of SMS pumping fraud.
